instruction: What does rule 3(1) state about the detailed estimate of the original work?
input: 3. Detailed estimate of the original work.-(1) Where the estimate of the cost for the execution of any original work on a national highway exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs, a detailed estimate of the cost for the execution of the work shall be forwarded by the executive agency to the Central Government in such form as the Central Government may specify in that behalf and that Government may accord technical approval and financial sanction to such estimate subject to such conditions as it may think fit to impose. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 3(1) states that if the cost estimate for executing any original work on a national highway exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs, the executive agency must forward a detailed cost estimate to the Central Government in a specified form. The Central Government may then grant technical approval and financial sanction to the estimate, subject to any conditions it deems necessary.

instruction: What is the procedure for works costing less than Rs. 10 lakhs according to rule 3(2)?
input: (2) Where the estimate of the cost for the execution of any original work on a national highway does not exceed Rs. 10 lakhs, technical approval and financial sanction to the plan and estimate for the execution of such work may be accorded by the executive agency concerned subject to the conditions specified in the Schedule annexed to these rules. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: For works costing less than Rs. 10 lakhs, rule 3(2) allows the executive agency to grant technical approval and financial sanction to the plan and estimate, provided it adheres to the conditions outlined in the Schedule attached to these rules.

instruction: What does rule 3(3) state about undertaking original work without approval?
input: (3) No original work on any national highway shall be undertaken by the executive agency until technical approval and financial sanction to the estimate for the execution of the work have been accorded by the Central Government or the executive agency, as the case may be, except in cases of emergency, such as flood, earthquake or any other force majeure which shall be immediately reported to the authority competent to sanction the estimate and the Audit Officer concerned indicating the approximate amount of liability involved. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 3(3) prohibits the executive agency from starting any original work on a national highway without first obtaining technical approval and financial sanction from the Central Government or the executive agency. However, in emergencies like floods, earthquakes, or other force majeure events, work can commence immediately, but the situation must be promptly reported to the competent authority and the Audit Officer, detailing the approximate liability.

instruction: What is required by rule 4 regarding the maintenance of national highways?
input: 4. Abstract of particulars of detailed estimate for maintenance of national highways.-An abstract of the particulars of the detailed estimate for the maintenance of a national highway during each financial year shall be forwarded by the executive agency to the Central Government in such form as the Central Government may require not later than the 1st day of the month of May in that financial year: Provided that the Central Government may, in any case or class of cases, require the executive agency to forward a detailed estimate or estimates for the maintenance of any national highway in such form as that Government may require. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 4 requires the executive agency to submit an abstract of the detailed estimate for maintaining a national highway each financial year to the Central Government by the 1st of May. The Central Government may also request detailed estimates for maintenance in specific cases or classes of cases, as it deems necessary.

instruction: What does rule 5(1) state about revised detailed estimates?
input: 5. Revised detailed estimate.-Where the expenditure upon any original work on a national highway for the detailed estimate of the cost for which the Central Government has accorded technical approval and financial sanction, under sub-rule (1) of rule 3, is likely at any time to exceed, or exceeds, the amount of such estimate by more than fifteen per cent. thereof or by a sum of one crore rupees, whichever is less, the executive agency shall forward a revised detailed estimate of the cost for such work to the Central Government in such form as that Government may specify in this behalf, and the Central Government may accord technical approval and financial sanction to the revised detailed estimate subject to such conditions as it may think fit to impose. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 5(1) states that if the expenditure on any original work on a national highway is likely to exceed or exceeds the approved estimate by more than fifteen percent or one crore rupees, whichever is less, the executive agency must submit a revised detailed estimate to the Central Government. The Central Government may then grant technical approval and financial sanction to the revised estimate, subject to any conditions it imposes.

instruction: What is the procedure for applying for allotment of funds according to rule 6?
input: 6. Application for allotment of funds.-An application for the allotment of funds for meeting expenditure on any original work on a national highway or on the maintenance of a national highway during any financial year shall be made by the executive agency to the Central Government in such form as that Government may require and the Central Government shall communicate its decision to the executive agency on such application as soon as possible after such application is received. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 6 outlines the procedure for applying for the allotment of funds, requiring the executive agency to submit an application to the Central Government in the specified form for funding original works or maintenance on national highways. The Central Government will then communicate its decision on the application as promptly as possible after receiving it.

instruction: What does rule 7 require regarding monthly progress reports?
input: 7. Monthly progress report.-The executive agency shall furnish to the Central Government a monthly progress report on every approved work in such form as that Government may require. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 7 mandates that the executive agency must provide the Central Government with a monthly progress report on every approved work, in the form specified by the Central Government.

instruction: What is required by rule 8 after the completion of an approved work?
input: 8. Completion report.-As early as possible after the completion of any approved work the executive agency shall furnish to the Central Government a full and correct report on such completion in such form as that Government may require. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 8 requires the executive agency to submit a full and accurate completion report to the Central Government as soon as possible after the completion of any approved work, in the form specified by the Central Government.

instruction: What does rule 9 state about the inspection of works?
input: 9. Inspection of works.-The Consulting Engineer to the Government of India (Road Development) or any officer authorised by him in this behalf may inspect at any time any approved work in progress or completed. A report of every such inspection shall be submitted to the Central Government. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 9 allows the Consulting Engineer to the Government of India (Road Development) or any authorized officer to inspect any approved work, whether in progress or completed, at any time. A report of each inspection must be submitted to the Central Government.

instruction: What does rule 10 state about the utilisation of space beneath the road, overbridges or flyovers?
input: 10. Utilisation of space beneath the road, overbridges or flyovers.-The Central Government, where it deems fit, may accord permission to the State Government or the Government of a Union Territory, as the case may be, for utilisation of space beneath the road, overbridges or flyovers on national highways for which an yearly licence fee which shall be either- (i) a percentage of capital cost; consisting of the cost of land and the cost, if any, incurred by the Central Government for covering or enclosing the space beneath the approach spans of road, overbridges or flyovers and for providing sanitary, water supply and electric installations, equal to such rate of interest as may from time to time be fixed by the President under FR 45A plus an addition for house or property tax, if any, payable by Government in respect of the covered space and for maintenance and repairs of the covered structure, or (ii) six per cent. per annum of such capital cost, whichever is less, shall be fixed and levied on the terms and conditions as may be laid down by the Central Government in this respect. The rate of licence fee to be levied as above, shall be subject to revision after every five years to take into account any change in the market value of the land. from The National Highways Rules_ 1957
output: Rule 10 allows the Central Government to permit the State Government or the Government of a Union Territory to use the space beneath roads, overbridges, or flyovers on national highways. An annual license fee will be charged, calculated as a percentage of the capital cost or six percent per annum of the capital cost, whichever is less. This fee includes costs for land, covering or enclosing the space, and providing sanitary, water supply, and electric installations, plus any applicable house or property tax and maintenance costs. The license fee rate is subject to revision every five years to reflect changes in land market value.

instruction: What does the term 'Act' refer to in these rules?
input: 2. Definitions.-In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) 'Act' means the National Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 1956); from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997

instruction: What is the definition of 'executing agency' in these rules?
input: (b) 'executing agency' means,- (i) in the case of those national highways administratively placed under the charge of Border Roads Organisation, the Border Roads Development Board (hereinafter referred to as 'BRDB'); (ii) in the case of those national highways or part thereof entrusted to National Highways Authority of India (hereinafter referred to as 'NHAI', the National Highways Authority of India; (iii) in other cases the State Government or Union Territory, the Administration to which such functions are delegated under section 5 of the Act; from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: The term 'executing agency' refers to: (i) the Border Roads Development Board (BRDB) for national highways under the Border Roads Organisation; (ii) the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for national highways or parts thereof entrusted to it; (iii) the State Government or Union Territory Administration to which functions are delegated under section 5 of the Act in other cases.

instruction: What does rule 3 state about the rate of fee and its payment?
input: 3. Rate of fee and its payment.-These shall be levied and paid to the executing agency, on behalf of the Government of India, fee on mechanical vehicles for the use of National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both at the rates notified by the Central Government, in the Official Gazette in respect of such National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 3 states that fees shall be levied and paid to the executing agency on behalf of the Government of India for mechanical vehicles using the National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both, at rates notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette.

instruction: What is required by rule 4 regarding the displaying of rates of fees?
input: 4. Displaying of rates of fees.-A table displaying rates of fees, rates authorised to be levied at any National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both shall be put up in a conspicuous place near the fee collection booths legibly written or printed in English, Hindi and the regional language of the area in which National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both are situated. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 4 requires that a table displaying the rates of fees authorized to be levied at any National Highway Section or permanent bridge or both shall be displayed in a conspicuous place near the fee collection booths, legibly written or printed in English, Hindi, and the regional language of the area.

instruction: What procedure does rule 5 establish for the collection of fees?
input: 5. Procedure for collection.-All fees levied under these rules shall be collected by the executing agency concerned departmentally or through private contractors on the basis of competitive bidding on behalf of the Central Government. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 5 establishes that all fees levied under these rules shall be collected by the executing agency either departmentally or through private contractors based on competitive bidding, on behalf of the Central Government.

instruction: What does rule 6(1) state about the collection of fees departmentally?
input: 6. Collection of fees departmentally.-(1) The executing agency concerned shall make necessary arrangement for putting up adequate number of collection booths, operated manually or by automatic arrangement or by combination of both as may be considered suitable by the executing agency. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 6(1) states that the executing agency shall arrange for an adequate number of collection booths, which may be operated manually, automatically, or a combination of both, as deemed suitable by the executing agency.

instruction: What is the mode of collection of fee in case of departmental fee collection as per rule 7(1)?
input: 7. Mode of collection of fee in case of departmental fee collection.(1) Every driver, owner or person incharge of a mechanical vehicle shall, before crossing the National Highway Section or permanent bridge or having crossed it, stop his vehicle at the cross bar and pay the fee leviable in respect of the vehicles at the fee collection booths. The Fee Inspector shall in return, prepare a receipt in duplicate in Form A and hand over one copy of the receipt to the driver or owner or person incharge of the mechanical vehicle. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 7(1) states that every driver, owner, or person in charge of a mechanical vehicle must stop at the cross bar before or after crossing the National Highway Section or permanent bridge to pay the applicable fee at the fee collection booths. The Fee Inspector will then prepare a duplicate receipt in Form A and give one copy to the driver, owner, or person in charge of the vehicle.

instruction: What does rule 8(1) state about the remittance of fee collection in case of departmental fee collection?
input: 8. Remittance of fee collection in case of departmental fee collection.(1) The Fee Inspector on duty shall be responsible for the collection and safe custody of the amounts collected during his duty period. The Fee Inspector shall not leave the collection booth till his reliever takes over from him. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 8(1) states that the Fee Inspector on duty is responsible for collecting and safely keeping the amounts collected during his duty period. The Fee Inspector must not leave the collection booth until his reliever takes over.

instruction: What is the procedure for fee collection through franchisee as per rule 9(1)?
input: 9. Fee collection through franchisee.-(1) In case the fee collection is to be done through the franchisee, the collection of fee and retaining such fee shall be auctioned under the instructions for specific periods as the Central Government may issue and the money shall be collected by the executing agency or his authorised representative as per the terms and conditions of the agreement executed for such purposes. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 9(1) states that if fee collection is to be done through a franchisee, the collection and retention of fees shall be auctioned according to instructions issued by the Central Government for specific periods. The money shall be collected by the executing agency or its authorized representative as per the terms and conditions of the agreement.

instruction: What does rule 10 state about special conditions when sections or bridges built by Government are used for developing adjacent Build, Operate and Transfer Projects of private parties?
input: 10. Special conditions when sections or bridges built by Government are used for developing adjacent Build, Operate and Transfer Projects of private parties.-To improve the financial viability of a Build, Operate and Transfer Project as decided by the Competent Authority, the concessionaire may be allowed to. collect and retain the fees so collected for the full concession period as agreed to in the specific agreement in respect of the facility offered to him under National Highways (Collection of Fee by any Person for the Use of Section of National Highways/Permanent Bridges/Temporary Bridges on National Highways) Rules, 1997 and the facility shall revert back to the Government at the end of concession period and the collection of fee thereafter shall be governed by these rules. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 10 states that to improve the financial viability of a Build, Operate and Transfer Project, the concessionaire may be allowed to collect and retain fees for the full concession period as agreed in the specific agreement. The facility shall revert to the Government at the end of the concession period, and fee collection thereafter shall be governed by these rules.

instruction: What is the tenure of fee collection as per rule 11?
input: 11. Tenure of fee collection.-The fee shall be collected in perpetuity by the executing agency. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 11 states that the fee shall be collected in perpetuity by the executing agency.

instruction: What does rule 12(1) require regarding the submission of returns in case of departmental fee collection?
input: 12. Submission of returns.-(1) The executing agency concerned in case of departmental fee collection shall furnish returns in the first week of July, October, January and April of every year to the Pay and Accounts Officer containing- (a) Monthwise consolidated statement showing the amount collected and remitted on account of fee proceeds in respect of each National Highway Section or permanent bridge alongwith the details of number and date of demand draft by which the amount has been remitted, and (b) Monthwise break up of the expenditure incurred on each National Highway Section or permanent bridge by the executing agency required to be reimbursed on account of collection of the fees on the basis of actual expenditure incurred. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 12(1) requires the executing agency to furnish returns in the first week of July, October, January, and April of every year to the Pay and Accounts Officer. These returns must include: (a) a month-wise consolidated statement of the amount collected and remitted for each National Highway Section or permanent bridge, including details of the demand draft used for remittance; and (b) a month-wise breakdown of the expenditure incurred on each National Highway Section or permanent bridge that needs to be reimbursed based on actual expenditure.

instruction: What is required by rule 13 regarding the furnishing of security in case of departmental fees collection?
input: 13. Furnishing of security in case of departmental fees collection.-Every Fee Inspector or the Sectional Officer/Junior Engineer-in-charge shall deposit a cash security of not less than Rs. 1000 by executing a security bond in the prescribed form as laid down in the Treasury Rules with the concerned Executive Engineer or the concerned officer of equivalent rank in any other department. from The National Highways _ Fee for the use of National Highways and Permanent Bridge _ Public Funded Project _ Rules_ 1997
output: Rule 13 requires every Fee Inspector or Sectional Officer/Junior Engineer-in-charge to deposit a cash security of not less than Rs. 1000 by executing a security bond in the prescribed form as per the Treasury Rules, with the concerned Executive Engineer or equivalent officer in any other department.

instruction: What does rule 3(1) state about the agreement and rate of fee?
input: 3. output: Rule 3(1) states that the Central Government may enter into an agreement with any person for the development and maintenance of the whole or any part of a national highway/permanent bridge/temporary bridge on national highway, allowing the person to invest his own funds for the development/maintenance and to collect and retain fees at agreed rates from different categories of mechanical vehicles for an agreed period, subject to the terms and conditions of the agreement and these rules.

instruction: How are the rates of fees and the period of collection decided according to rule 3(2)?
input: 3. Agreement and rate of fee.-(2) The rates of fees and the period of collection shall be decided and shall be specified by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government having regard to the expenditure involved in building, maintenance, management and operation of the whole or part of such section, interest on the capital invested, reasonable return, the volume of traffic and the period of such agreement.
output: According to rule 3(2), the rates of fees and the period of collection are decided and specified by notification in the Official Gazette by the Central Government, considering the expenditure involved in building, maintenance, management and operation of the whole or part of such section, interest on the capital invested, reasonable return, the volume of traffic and the period of such agreement.

instruction: What happens upon completion of the period of collection of fees by the person as per rule 3(3)?

output: Upon completion of the period of collection of fees by the person, as per rule 3(3), all rights pertaining to the section/permanent bridge/temporary bridge on national highway are deemed to have been taken over by the Central Government, which shall continue with the collection of fees as notified from time to time.

instruction: What responsibilities does the in-charge of fee collection have according to rule 5(1)?

Incharge of fee collection.- ${ }^{2}[(1)$ The person authorised to collect and retain the fees under these rules shall nominate an official as in-charge of fee collection, and the person as also the official so nominated shall be responsible to ensure that fees are collected at not more than the agreed rates and the fee collection is smooth without causing undue hardship to the road users, and for all other matters connected with the fee collection of section of national highway/permanent bridge/temporary bridge:

instruction: What vehicles are exempt from paying fees as per rule 5(1)?
input: 5. Incharge of fee collection.- Provided that no fee shall be payable or collected in respect of the following vehicles, namely:- ${ }^{3}[(\mathrm{i})$ vehicles- (A) having 'VIP' symbols; or officially belonging to- (a) President of India; (b) Vice-President of India; (c) Governor of a State or Lt. Governor of a Union Territory; (d) a Foreign Dignitary on State visit to India; (e) a foreign diplomat stationed in India using cars with 'CD'/ 'CC' number plates; (f) Chairman of Rajya Sabha or Speaker of Lok Sabha or Chairman of a State Legislative Council or Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly or a Minister for the union or State, or Leaders of Opposition in Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha or State Legislatures having the status of Cabinet Minister, if he is sitting in the vehicle; or (g) a Member of Parliament, in the entire country, or a Member of Legislative Assembly of a State or a Member of Legislative Council of a State, in the respective State, if he produces his identity card issued by the Parliament or concerned Legislature of a State, as the case may be; (B) belonging to winner of Gallantry awards such as Param. Governor of a Union Territory, a Foreign Dignitary on State visit to India, foreign diplomats stationed in India using cars with 'CD'/'CC' number plates, Chairman of Rajya Sabha or Speaker of Lok Sabha or Chairman of a State Legislative Council or Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly or a Minister for the union or State, or Leaders of Opposition in Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha or State Legislatures having the status of Cabinet Minister if sitting in the vehicle, Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assembly of a State or Members of Legislative Council of a State if they produce their identity card, vehicles belonging to winners of Gallantry awards if they produce their photo identity card duly authenticated, and Defence vehicles, Police vehicles, Fire-fighting vehicles, Ambulances, Funeral vans, Posts and Telegraphs Department vehicles, and Central Government and State Government vehicles on duty.

instruction: What must be displayed regarding the in-charge of fee collection according to rule 5(2)?

instruction: What is the responsibility of the person referred to in rule 3(1) regarding fee collection verification as per rule 6(1)?

The auditor shall be appointed by the Government.

output: Subject to provisions of the Act, the executing agency authorised by the Central Government in this behalf, shall open and maintain an account with one or more Scheduled Commercial Banks for remittance of the amount for land acquisition across the country, with arrangements for access to such account by the competent authority for specific jurisdiction as per authorisation of limits by the executing agency.

instruction: What is the procedure for disbursement of the compensation amount to the landowners or persons interested therein as per rule 3(i)?
input: rule 3(i) from The National Highways _Manner of deposition_ Rules_ 2018
output: The Executing Agency shall, on the demand raised by the competent authority before announcement of the award, issue requisite authorisation limits in favour of the competent authority for withdrawal of amount from such account as per requirements from time to time for disbursement to the landowners or persons interested therein through an electronic banking mechanism as per extant Reserve Bank of India regulations and the said authorisation limits, revolving in nature, shall entitle the competent authority to withdraw money from such account as per requirements, without any further reference to the land acquiring agency, for disbursement to the landowners or persons interested therein.

instruction: What does rule 3(ii) state about the maintenance of the requisite account by the executing agency?
input: rule 3(ii) from The National Highways _Manner of deposition_ Rules_ 2018
output: The executing agency, authorised by the Central Government in this behalf, shall ensure that the requisite account is maintained with a Scheduled Commercial Bank, against which an authorisation limit is issued in favour of the competent authority for disbursement of the compensation amount, duly determined under Section 3(G) of the Act, to the landowners or persons interested therein.

instruction: What is the procedure for disbursement of the compensation amount in cases where the executing agency of a project is any State Government or Union territory as per rule 3(iii)?
input: rule 3(iii) from The National Highways _Manner of deposition_ Rules_ 2018
output: In cases where the executing agency of a project is any State Government or Union territory, the amount shall preferably be disbursed through the Public Financial Management System of the Ministry of Finance.

instruction: What does rule 3(iv) state about the disbursement of the compensation amount to the landowners or the persons interested therein?
input: rule 3(iv) from The National Highways _Manner of deposition_ Rules_ 2018
output: The competent authority shall, in turn, disburse the compensation amount to the landowners or the persons interested therein preferably by electronically crediting the said amount into their respective bank accounts.

instruction: What does rule 4 state about the undisbursed amounts due to disputes?
input: rule 4 from The National Highways _Manner of deposition_ Rules_ 2018
output: Where the amount deposited earlier by the executing agency into the account of the competent authority has remained undisbursed, or where the authorisation limit for an account has been issued in favour of the competent authority for disbursement purposes but certain amounts remain undisbursed, due to disputes which are referable to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction for resolution in terms of sub-section (4) of section 3H of the National Highways Act, 1956, the competent authority shall, while forwarding such references to the Court, cause such undisbursed amounts to be deposited with the principal court of civil jurisdiction to whom any such disputes are referable, for payment to entitled persons as and when the said disputes are resolved, or the absentee title-holders submit their claims, as the case may be, such amounts deposited with the principal court of civil jurisdiction shall, for all purposes, be deemed as payment made to entitled persons under sub-section (2) of section 3 H of the Act.

instruction: What is the short title and commencement of the National Highways (Rate of Fee) Rules, 1997?
input: 1. Short title and commencement.-(1) These rules may be called the National Highways (Rate of Fee) Rules, 1997. (2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: The short title of these rules is the National Highways (Rate of Fee) Rules, 1997. They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

instruction: What does the term 'Act' refer to in these rules?
input: (a) 'Act' means the National Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 1956); from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: In these rules, the term 'Act' refers to the National Highways Act, 1956 (48 of 1956).

instruction: Define 'mechanical vehicle' as per these rules.
input: (b) 'mechanical vehicle' means any laden or unladen vehicle designed to be driven under its own power, including a motor vehicle as defined in clause (28) of section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (59 of 1988); from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: A 'mechanical vehicle' is defined as any laden or unladen vehicle designed to be driven under its own power, including a motor vehicle as defined in clause (28) of section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (59 of 1988).

instruction: What is the definition of 'bridge' according to these rules?
input: (c) 'bridge' means a permanent bridge or a temporary bridge, as the case may be, the cost of which includes the cost of bridge proper, approach roads, guide bunds and protective works, excluding the cost of toll booths, which is more than rupees 25 lakhs and upto rupees 100 lakh for each, completed and opened to traffic on or after first day of April 1976 but before the first day of May, 1992 and thereafter all the bridges costing more than Rs. 100 lakhs before the date of the publication of this notification in the Official Gazette and thereafter all the bridges costing more than Rs. 500 lakhs on National Highways, which shall be notified separately for levy of fee collection; from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: A 'bridge' is defined as a permanent bridge or a temporary bridge, the cost of which includes the cost of bridge proper, approach roads, guide bunds and protective works, excluding the cost of toll booths. It must cost more than rupees 25 lakhs and up to rupees 100 lakh for each, completed and opened to traffic on or after the first day of April 1976 but before the first day of May, 1992. Thereafter, all bridges costing more than Rs. 100 lakhs before the date of the publication of this notification in the Official Gazette and all bridges costing more than Rs. 500 lakhs on National Highways, which shall be notified separately for levy of fee collection.

instruction: What does 'section of national highway or permanent bridge or temporary bridge' mean?
input: (d) 'section of national highway or permanent bridge or temporary bridge' means that continuous length of national highway or permanent bridge or temporary bridge on national highway as notified by the Central Government in Official Gazette on which fee shall be charged. from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: A 'section of national highway or permanent bridge or temporary bridge' refers to the continuous length of national highway or permanent bridge or temporary bridge on national highway as notified by the Central Government in the Official Gazette on which fee shall be charged.

instruction: How often may the rate of fee fixed under sub-rule (1) and sub-rule (2) be reviewed?
input: ${ }^{1}[(3)$ The rate of fee fixed under sub-rule (1) and sub-rule (2) may be reviewed after every five years based on wholesale price index and fixed in multiple of rupees five by the Central Government over the rates notified.] from The National Highways _Rate of Fee_ Rules_ 1997
output: The rate of fee fixed under sub-rule (1) and sub-rule (2) may be reviewed after every five years based on the wholesale price index and fixed in multiples of rupees five by the Central Government over the rates notified.

instruction: What does rule 1(1) state about the short title and commencement?
input: 1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: Rule 1(1) states that these rules may be called the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008.

instruction: What is the definition of 'Act' as per rule 2(1)(a)?
input: 2. Definitions.-(1)'In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) 'Act' means the National Highways Act, 1956; from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 2(1)(a), 'Act' means the National Highways Act, 1956.

instruction: What does rule 3(1) state about the levy of fee?
input: 3. Levy of fee.- (1) The Central Government may by notification, levy fee for use of any section of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel forming part of the national highway, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of these rules: from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: Rule 3(1) states that the Central Government may by notification, levy fee for use of any section of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel forming part of the national highway, as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions of these rules.

instruction: What is the base rate of fee for a car, jeep, van, or light motor vehicle as per rule 4(2)?

output: The base rate of fee for a car, jeep, van, or light motor vehicle as per rule 4(2) is 0.65 Rupees per km.

instruction: What does rule 5(1) state about the annual revision of rate of fee?
input: 5. Annual revision of rate of fee.-(1) The rates specified under rule 4 shall be increased without compounding, by three per cent. each year with effect from the $1^{\text {st }}$ day of April, 2008 and such increased rate shall be deemed to be the base rate for the subsequent years. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: Rule 5(1) states that the rates specified under rule 4 shall be increased without compounding, by three per cent. each year with effect from the 1st day of April, 2008 and such increased rate shall be deemed to be the base rate for the subsequent years.

instruction: What is the procedure for collection of fee as per rule 6(1)?
input: 6. Collection of fee.- (1) Fee levied under these rules shall be collected by the Central Government or the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, at the toll plaza. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 6(1), fee levied under these rules shall be collected by the Central Government or the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, at the toll plaza.

instruction: What does rule 7(1) state about the remittance and appropriation of fee?
input: 7. Remittance and appropriation of fee.- (1) In case of public funded projects, the fee collected under the provisions of these rules by every executing authority shall be remitted to the Central Government: from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: Rule 7(1) states that in case of public funded projects, the fee collected under the provisions of these rules by every executing authority shall be remitted to the Central Government.

instruction: What are the requirements for the location of a toll plaza as per rule 8(1)?
input: 8. Location of toll plaza.- (1) The executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, shall establish a toll plaza beyond a distance of ten kilometers from a municipal or local town area limits: from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 8(1), the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, shall establish a toll plaza beyond a distance of ten kilometers from a municipal or local town area limits.

instruction: What is the rate of fee for overloading as per rule 10(1)?
input: 10. Rate of fee for overloading.- (1) Without prejudice to the liability of the driver, owner or a person in charge of a mechanical vehicle under any law for the time being in force, a mechanical vehicle which is loaded in excess of the permissible load specified for its category under sub-rule (2) of rule 4 , shall be liable to pay fee at such rate which is applicable for the next higher category of mechanical vehicles: from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: Rule 10(1) states that a mechanical vehicle which is loaded in excess of the permissible load specified for its category under sub-rule (2) of rule 4, shall be liable to pay fee at such rate which is applicable for the next higher category of mechanical vehicles.

instruction: What exemptions from payment of fee are provided as per rule 11(1)?
input: 11. Exemption from payment of fee.- (1) No fee shall be levied and collected from a mechanical vehicle,- (a) transporting and accompanying,- (i) the President of India; (ii) the Vice-President of India; (iii) the Prime-Minister of India; (iv) the Chief Justice of India; (v) the Governor; (vi) the Lieutenant Governor; (vii) the Union Minister; (viii) the Chief Minister; (ix) the Judge of Supreme Court; (x) the Chairman of the Council of State; (xi) the Speaker of the House of People; (xii) the Chairman of the Legislative Council of the State; (xiii) the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of the State; (xiv) the Chief Justice of High Court; (xv) the Judge of High Court; (xvi) Ministers of States; and (xvii) Foreign dignitaries on State visit. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 11(1), no fee shall be levied and collected from a mechanical vehicle transporting and accompanying the President of India, the Vice-President of India, the Prime-Minister of India, the Chief Justice of India, the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor, the Union Minister, the Chief Minister, the Judge of Supreme Court, the Chairman of the Council of State, the Speaker of the House of People, the Chairman of the Legislative Council of the State, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly of the State, the Chief Justice of High Court, the Judge of High Court, Ministers of States, and Foreign dignitaries on State visit.

instruction: What information must be displayed as per rule 12(2)?
input: (2) The executing authority shall prominently display in Hindi and English one thousand meters ahead of the toll plaza and in English and local language five hundred meters ahead of the toll plaza,- (i) the amount of fee payable for each class of vehicles and the discounts available under rule 9 ; $L_{1} \beta \circ \beta$ o. $x / \mathrm{r} \beta-\mathrm{L} /$ (ii) the categories of vehicles exempted from payment of fee; and (iii) the name, address and telephone or contact number of the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 12(2), the executing authority shall prominently display in Hindi and English one thousand meters ahead of the toll plaza and in English and local language five hundred meters ahead of the toll plaza, the amount of fee payable for each class of vehicles and the discounts available under rule 9, the categories of vehicles exempted from payment of fee, and the name, address and telephone or contact number of the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be.

instruction: What is the procedure for unauthorized collection as per rule 13(1)?
input: 13. Unauthorised collection.- (1) An officer authorised by the Central Government or by the executing authority, as the case may be, may assess the excess fee collected, if any, by the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, and recover the same from such authority or concessionaire, along with an additional sum equal to twenty five per cent. of the excess fee collected: from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 13(1), an officer authorised by the Central Government or by the executing authority, as the case may be, may assess the excess fee collected, if any, by the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, and recover the same from such authority or concessionaire, along with an additional sum equal to twenty five per cent. of the excess fee collected.

instruction: What are the consequences of failure to pay fee as per rule 14(1)?
input: 14. Failure to pay fee.- (1) If any driver, owner or person in charge of a mechanical vehicle does not pay or refuses to pay the fee for use of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel, his or her vehicle shall not be allowed to use such section of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel and in case such vehicle obstructs the normal flow of traffic, the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, may get such obstructing vehicle removed from the national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel, as the case may be. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 14(1), if any driver, owner or person in charge of a mechanical vehicle does not pay or refuses to pay the fee for use of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel, his or her vehicle shall not be allowed to use such section of national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel and in case such vehicle obstructs the normal flow of traffic, the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be, may get such obstructing vehicle removed from the national highway, permanent bridge, bypass or tunnel, as the case may be.

instruction: What power does the Central Government have to verify records as per rule 15?
input: 15. Power of Central Government to verify records.- An officer duly authorised by the Central Government or the executing authority, as the case may be shall have the power to verify the collection of fee, and inspect any document, records, other information, receipts or reports of the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be. from The principal rules of the National Highways Fee _Determination of Rates and Collection_ Rules_ 2008
output: As per rule 15, an officer duly authorised by the Central Government or the executing authority, as the case may be, shall have the power to verify the collection of fee, and inspect any document, records, other information, receipts or reports of the executing authority or the concessionaire, as the case may be.
